summary: All six libraries registered as normal glucose match the high-glucose sheet in the [publisher’s supplement](https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/app152312391/s1). Across 11,703 paired genes, 98.83% agree in direction with that sheet and 45.43% with the published normal-glucose sheet. The glucose assignment remains unresolved, so the proposal includes no automated comparison spec or full-verification sign-off.
openIssues: Which GSM and MO library IDs came from the 5.5 mM and 25 mM glucose wells? The authors’ plate-to-library key would resolve the conflicting labels.
Which count file produced S1 column N3_2? It matches none of the deposited profiles, and the count file for GSM8487287 duplicates GSM8487285.
The paper reports 18 genes for each high-dose comparison. Applying its stated adjusted-P cutoff to S1 yields 17 for normal glucose and 16 for high glucose.
The methods do not establish whether the three RNA profiles per arm came from independent culture preparations.
